subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet you and Alicia. Quick recap and the procurement questions we promised to confirm so you can route internally: 

- Use case: internal search + support assistant (prod traffic expected Q4)
- Expected spend: $60k/year first 12 months (pilot month-to-month, scale after proof-of-value)
- Technical asks: SOC 2 type II report, basic KMS alignment, data retention controls

Commercial / procurement questions: 
1) Do you require a Purchase Order for all vendors, or is card payment allowed up to a threshold?
2) Is prepay accepted (customer wants to prepay to simplify billing this fiscal year)?
3) Would a purchase via Acme Marketplace expedite procurement?
4) Any vendor onboarding forms/documentation we should fill before legal review?

I've attached a short SOW draft and happy to provide the SOC2 + KMS writeup immediately if helpful. If a PO is required and Acme has a minimum contract spend or standard SLA exceptions process, let us know timeline expectations — we can be flexible on billing cadence to get started.

Next steps: Please loop in procurement (and ops) with any required forms — I'll follow up with the SOW and the SOC2 artifact.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions

Ben — thanks for the recap and SOW. Quick answers from procurement side after a brief sync with our team: 

- We generally require a PO for any vendor engagement. However, with procurement approval we can allow card payments up to a $20,000 threshold for business-critical SaaS vendors. For anything above that we need a PO and standard vendor onboarding.
- Acme does not typically accept prepay for new vendors (policy). Prepay requests go through an exceptions committee and are rare; timeline is 2-3 weeks for review.
- Marketplace purchases are often faster because vendor risk/onboarding is pre-validated, so yes, that would be preferred if Redwood is available in our marketplace.

To move forward we need: 
1) Completed vendor onboarding form (I'll attach the form)
2) W-9 (for US tax)
3) SOC 2 Type II report and data handling summary (KMS/retention)

Please note: I attached a copy of our PO policy (Acme_PO_policy.pdf) — it lists thresholds and approval flows. If Redwood cannot accept a PO, please flag as an exception request and provide a business justification and estimated spend profile.

Appreciate it — looping in Alicia (ops lead) for any marketplace-specific questions.

—Sanjay
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions

Sanjay — thanks for the clarity and the PO policy. Attaching the SOC2 summary + our W-9 now (SOC2 doc to follow via secure link).

Couple of follow-ups from our side: 
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed in the AWS and GCP marketplaces under Redwood Inference. If Acme can purchase via marketplace that will remove the vendor onboarding friction. I'll send the marketplace listing links and pricing SKU IDs if you'd like.
- Prepay: The customer indicated a preference to prepay to keep their FY22 books tidy. We understand it's not standard but wanted to raise it as a possible short-term workaround if your exceptions committee will entertain it. We can offer a prepay invoice and an escrow-style hold if that helps.
- PO exceptions: if a PO is strictly required for this spend level, can procurement confirm the expected vendor onboarding timeline (we're seeing ~7-10 business days for vendor form review in similar accounts, but would like your internal estimate).

I attached a short SOW and our draft commercial terms to expedite legal review (Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf). Marissa is copied to help with any redlines.

If it helps, we're happy to go live with a pilot on card up to $20k while the larger PO runs through the onboarding — would that be an acceptable interim path?

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions

Hi Sanjay / Alicia — Marissa here (copied Ben earlier) — I'm the AE who will help move commercial/contract items. A few notes from our side to speed the process: 

- We can complete your vendor onboarding form immediately and provide the SOC 2 Type II report + KMS write-up via secure link.
- Redwood Finance can support a single invoice prepay if Acme's exceptions committee needs a clear payment instrument to approve. I cannot promise policy exceptions, but we will provide whatever artifacts your committee requires (business justification, scope of prepay, refund terms).
- Pilot suggestion: If Acme permits, run the initial pilot (<$20k) on card to unblock the POC while the full vendor onboarding + PO are processed. We will provide an estimated monthly spend cadence to make approvals easier.

Next steps from us: Ben will share the secure SOC2 link and W-9; I'll send a clean SOW with tracked terms for your legal. If you can send the vendor form today, I'll prioritize it with Finance/legal so we can get initial approvals in 3-5 business days.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path & exceptions

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. A few confirmations from ops/procurement: 

- Marketplace: Redwood is listed in our marketplace but not yet in our Vendor Registry. Marketplace purchase is preferred and will be the fastest route, but procurement needs Redwood to complete the Vendor Registry intake to enable marketplace checkout on our side. Link to intake: https://vendor-portal.acme.com/onboarding/req-449
- Card vs PO: We can approve card payments up to $25k for vendors that complete the Vendor Registry and pass a quick risk check. Above $25k requires a PO.
- Prepay: Our exceptions committee will review prepay requests but requires "business justification + refund/termination terms" from the vendor. Expect a 7-10 business day review window for that exception.
- Required docs: SOC2 Type II, W-9, and a signed SOW/contract (or DocuSign link) for initial invoicing.

Next steps: If Redwood can fill the Vendor Registry intake (once you confirm a point of contact I'll provide access), procurement will run a prioritized review. For speed we recommend: 1) complete intake, 2) marketplace checkout for pilot under $25k, 3) run PO onboarding in parallel for the larger commit.

I'll start the vendor exception packet internally in case prepay is needed — please send the business justification text and proposed refund terms.

Thanks — Alicia
